sections.title: Design Specification
sections.content:
**Overview**

Retrieve source code definitions from files by name, caching definitions and file content to enable efficient lookup of function, class, and variable implementations across a project.

- Call `file_definition()` to look up a single definition by name in a file and get its metadata; call `source_definition()` to get both the definition metadata and its source text.
- Call `extract_callee_source()` to retrieve the complete source code of a definition by name from a dependency target file, handling special cases for COBOL, BMS, and R languages.
- Call `extract_definition_source()` when you know a definition's start line to retrieve its source text, falling back to `extract_callee_source()` if that lookup fails.
- Call `file_definition_list()` to get all definitions of a file cached and parsed once, or `file_content()` to read file UTF-8 text without parsing.
- Call `clear_definition_source_cache()` to flush all cached definitions and file content between analysis runs.

This module depends on `codetwine/parsers/ts_parser.py` for parsing files and reading UTF-8 content, on `codetwine/extractors/definitions.py` to extract definition metadata from ASTs, and on `codetwine/extractors/r_source.py` and `codetwine/config/settings.py` for language-specific handling. It is used by `codetwine/file_analyzer.py` and `codetwine/import_binding.py` to retrieve definitions for analysis, by `codetwine/import_reference.py` to resolve imported names, and by `codetwine/extractors/usage_analysis.py` and `codetwine/extractors/dependency_graph.py` to look up definitions during reference tracking.

The module maintains three independent caches: one for definitions with file content (bounded by `PARSE_CACHE_MAX_FILES`), one for definitions without content (unbounded), and one for definition indexes (name lookups) keyed by Python object identity. Definitions are never modified by callers; all lists returned from cache are shared and must not be altered. COBOL, BMS, and R files return None from lookup functions because their definitions lack byte offsets required for source text extraction.

**Definitions**

## `_definition_cache`

Module-level OrderedDict caching definitions and UTF-8 file content together, ordered from least to most recently used and bounded by `PARSE_CACHE_MAX_FILES` to limit memory. When the cache is full, the oldest entry is evicted and must be re-parsed on next lookup.

## `_definition_list_cache`

Module-level dictionary caching definitions without associated file content for languages that do not parse into syntax trees (COBOL, BMS, R). Unlike `_definition_cache`, this cache has no size limit.

## `_definition_index_cache`

Module-level dictionary caching name-to-definitions lookups and top-level definition IDs for each definition list, keyed by Python object identity of the list to detect when the same list object is reused. Indexed cache entries are tuple triples of (the list, name-to-definitions mapping, top-level definition IDs).

## `clear_definition_source_cache`

Forget all cached definitions, file content, and name indexes. Called by dependency graph analysis to reset state between analysis runs.

## `_definition_index`

Build and cache name-to-definitions lookup and top-level definition ID set for a definition list once per list object. Uses Python object identity to detect cache reuse; returns a tuple of the name mapping (name string to list of definitions with that name in line order) and the set of object IDs of top-level definitions that `select_top_level_definitions()` retains.

## `file_definition_list`

Return cached definitions of a file extracted once per file and without its syntax tree. Calls `extract_definitions()` with the specified `definition_dict` for the file's language, then stores the result in `_definition_list_cache` to avoid re-extracting on subsequent calls. The returned list is shared and must not be modified.

## `file_content`

Return UTF-8 text of a file as bytes, preferring cached parse results from `parse_cache` and falling back to `read_utf8_content()` for files not yet parsed. Does not parse the file.

## `_file_definition`

Return definitions and UTF-8 content of a file together, keeping them paired in `_definition_cache` while the file remains in cache. Implements LRU eviction by moving accessed entries to the end and removing the oldest when the cache exceeds `PARSE_CACHE_MAX_FILES`. Calls `file_definition_list()` and `file_content()` separately then stores their results as a tuple.

## `_is_inside`

Test whether a definition's lines fall entirely within the lines of any owner definition in a list. Used to determine nesting of definitions inside classes, impl blocks, or other containers.

## `_find_by_path`

Follow parts of a name through nested definitions by walking from top-level definitions into those written inside them. Returns the definition reached by the last part, preferring non-attached definitions (those not in `ATTACHED_DEFINITION_TYPE_SET`) and top-level definitions for the first part. Stops at the first part that names no definition and returns None if the first part itself names nothing.

## `find_definition`

Find a definition in a file by a name with parts joined by "." or "::", trying first as a whole name then walking through parts via `_find_by_path()`. Skips leading parts that are not file definitions (modules, namespaces, variables).

## `file_definition`

Return the definition metadata that a name names in a file, or None for files without language support or when the name is not found. Wrapper around `source_definition()` that discards the source text and returns only the definition.

## `source_definition`

Return both definition metadata and source text for a name in a file, with optional start line to disambiguate when multiple definitions share the same name. When `start_line` is provided, parts of the name are tried in reverse order to find a definition starting at that line; without it, `find_definition()` looks up the name. Returns None for COBOL, BMS, R files, or when the name is not found. Byte offsets from the definition are decoded as UTF-8 to extract the source text.

## `extract_callee_source`

Retrieve the complete source code of a definition by name from a file as a dependency target, handling COBOL files via their definition_source method, R files via `r_definition_text()`, and other languages via `source_definition()`. Returns None if the definition is not found or the file has no language support.

## `extract_definition_source`

Return the source text of a definition that starts on a specified line in a file, using `source_definition()` with the start line then falling back to `extract_callee_source()` if the line-based lookup returns None. Used to retrieve definition source when the line number is known and avoids ambiguity.

summary:
# Summary: codetwine/extractors/definition_source.py

**Single Responsibility:** Cache and retrieve source code definitions from files by name, providing efficient lookup of function, class, and variable implementations across a project with language-specific handling.

**Main Public Definitions:** `file_definition()`, `source_definition()`, `extract_callee_source()`, `extract_definition_source()`, `file_definition_list()`, `file_content()`, `clear_definition_source_cache()`, `find_definition()`.

**Key Terms:** Definition caching (LRU-bounded for parsed files, unbounded for unparsed), name-to-definition indexing, UTF-8 file content, syntax tree parsing, nested definition lookup via dotted/scoped paths, special handling for COBOL/BMS/R languages, byte offset decoding for source text extraction, dependency analysis support.
